titulo_ja: ふだん の はなし (2)

なく.es: no (forma negativa de だ, usada para unir)
なく.en: no (negative form of, used to unite)

texto: To add something that surprises, after what you already know: name or phrase + **ばかり か**: **かれ は べんきょう ばかり か、 スポーツ も じょうず です** (he not only studies, he is also good in sports).
It sounds like surprise or praise.
To add something to what has already been said, without the surprise: name + **だけ で なく**: **にほんご だけ で なく、 えいご も はなせます** (not only Japanese, I also speak English).
It is more neutral than **ばかりか**, although the emphasis depends on the phrase.

filas: べんきょう ばかりか
にほんご だけ で なく

frases.ja: かれ は べんきょう ばかり か、 スポーツ も じょうず です。

frases.en: He's not only a student, he's also good at sports.

frases.ja: にほんご だけ で なく、 えいご も はなせます。
frases.es: No solo hablo japonés, también hablo inglés.
frases.en: I don't just speak Japanese, I also speak English.

frases.es: Ella no solo canta bien, sino que también sabe tocar instrumentos. El año pasado ganó un premio en un concurso de música. A mucha gente le gusta verla seguir practicando.
frases.en: She not only sings well, she also knows how to play instruments. Last year he won an award in a music contest. A lot of people like to see her continue to practice.
